message.content: We don’t have a definitive answer for the “largest planet in the universe” because our observations are limited to the planets we’ve discovered so far. Among the exoplanets that have been measured, the biggest one we know of is **HD 100546 b**, a protoplanet still forming around a young star. It’s estimated to be roughly 10–20 times the mass of Jupiter and has a radius several times larger than Jupiter’s, making it the most massive planet we’ve detected to date. However, there may be even larger planets out there that we haven’t yet found or confirmed.
